site.name: openplate
site.tagline: An open-source food diary that runs on your device.
site.exampleData: These screens show example data, not a real diary.

hero.body: openplate is an open-source food diary that runs on your device, with an optional photo scan that estimates the macros on your plate. It is for people who want to track what they eat without sending their diary to someone else's server.
hero.lead: It is for people who want to track what they eat without sending their diary to someone else's server.
hero.inviteNote: The hosted instance is invite-only. Running your own copy needs no invitation.
hero.shotAlt: The openplate diary for one day: a ring showing the net carbs left of the daily limit, the protein count, and the meals logged under breakfast and lunch.

add.title: Log a food
add.body: Search the food database, or pick something you logged before, and the entry lands in the day under the meal you chose.
add.alt: The add-food screen: a search box, a button to scan the plate instead, and a list of recently logged foods with their net carbs.

scan.title: Scan a plate
scan.body: Photograph the plate and the AI service you connected estimates the carbs. The photo goes to that service and to nowhere else.
scan.alt: The scan screen, offering to connect an AI provider before it reads a photo, and a way to log the food without one.

goals.title: Set the targets
goals.body: A daily carb limit and a protein target, or neither. Every goal is optional and clearing a field removes it.
goals.alt: The goals screen: a daily net carb limit with preset choices and a custom field, and a protein target in grams.

overview.title: See where the day stands
overview.body: How much of the limit is left, whether the protein target is met, and how many of the last seven days you logged.
overview.alt: The overview screen: a ring showing the net carbs left of the daily limit, the protein count, and a card for the last seven days.

access.heading: Access
access.body: The hosted instance at openplate.de is invite-only. An administrator sends the invitation; there is no open sign-up. If you would rather run your own copy, see <selfHosting>Self-hosting</selfHosting>.

openSource.heading: Open source
openSource.body: openplate and openplate-sync are MIT licensed. openplate-inference carries its own terms, set by the model weights it ships; its licensing guide lists them. Read the code, change it, run it yourself: <repoApp>github.com/LowCarbCheck/openplate</repoApp>, <repoSync>github.com/LowCarbCheck/openplate-sync</repoSync>, <repoInference>github.com/LowCarbCheck/openplate-inference</repoInference>.

app.title: The app
app.lead: openplate logs food and, if you want it, estimates the macros on a plate from a photo. Search a food or scan a plate, and the entry lands in your diary for the day. On your own install, there is no sign-up screen: open the app and start logging. On the hosted instance, you sign in first.
app.shotIntro: The diary is one day at a time: the meals you logged, what they cost against the day's limit, and what is left of it.
app.shotAlt: The openplate diary on a phone: a ring showing the net carbs left of the daily limit, the protein count, and the day's meals grouped under breakfast and lunch.

stores.heading: What it stores on the device

sync.title: The sync server
sync.lead: openplate-sync carries your diary between your own devices. It stores an email address, an encrypted blob of your diary that it cannot read, and a recovery code sealed for the one case a forgotten password needs it.

inference.title: The inference runtime
inference.lead: openplate-inference is a plate-photo scanner you run on your own hardware. It names the foods on a plate and estimates the grams, then looks up the macros in a bundled food database rather than inventing numbers.

audience.heading: Who it is for
audience.body: Self-hosters who want plate scans with no cloud AI account and no photo leaving their network. It is not part of the hosted instance at openplate.de.

deploy.title: How to run openplate
deploy.lead: You can use openplate without running anything at all, and you can run every part of it yourself. Four rungs sit between those two. Each rung adds a capability and adds something you now have to operate, so read it as a ladder you are meant to stop climbing early.

rung0.heading: Use an instance someone else runs

rung1.heading: Run the app on your own box

docs.title: Documentation
docs.intro: These pages document all three services: the app, the sync server, and the self-hosted inference runtime. Start with the service you are running, or with Self-hosting if you are starting from nothing.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.body: This site uses Matomo without cookies to count visits; it does not track you across sites or build a profile of you. There are no accounts on this site itself; invite-only accounts belong to the hosted app, not to openplate.de. For what the app stores and sends, see the app's own privacy page, linked from within the app.
